baseline.level: Celery worker control, not application stop
baseline.scope: Skip revoked tasks if the worker knows the task ID; does not stop a task already executing.
baseline.durable_comparator: The same worker configuration with a declared persistent --statedb file.

default_native_worker_config.task_reject_on_worker_lost: Celery default False; not overridden by workers/celery_app.py
default_native_worker_config.worker_state_db: Celery default None; not configured in documented worker command

baseline.child_loss_qualification: Do not infer redelivery from acks_late alone; task_reject_on_worker_lost and task_process/whole_worker loss must be distinguished.
baseline.restart_qualification: Distinguish restart of all workers from a worker that can synchronize revokes from surviving peers.

qualifications: Plain revoke does not terminate an already-running task.
Revoked IDs are normally in memory; restarting all workers can lose them absent persistent state, while surviving peers can synchronize revokes.
Killing a task pool child is normally acknowledged even with late acks when reject_on_worker_lost is false; do not conflate it with whole-worker or broker connection loss.
Whole-worker loss/redelivery depends on acknowledgement and broker visibility/recovery conditions; Redis default visibility timeout is one hour.
